stem.text: A curve is defined by \( 4\left(y - 1\right)^{2} = \left(x + 4\right)^{2}\left(x - 8\right) \), and its derivative is \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\left(x + 4\right)\left(3x - 12\right)}{8\left(y - 1\right)} \). Find every point of the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal, or show that there is none.

answer_key.label: No point of the curve has a horizontal tangent line.

worked_solution.text: A horizontal tangent needs the numerator of dy/dx to be 0 and the denominator to be nonzero. The numerator is 0 when \( x = -4 \) or \( x = 4 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator of dy/dx equal to zero

worked_solution.text: On the curve, \( x = -4 \) forces \( y = 1 \), where the denominator is also 0, so \( (-4, 1) \) is not a point with a horizontal tangent.
Substituting \( x = 4 \) into the curve gives \( \left(y - 1\right)^{2} = -64 \), which no real y satisfies. There is no point of the curve with a horizontal tangent line.

options.label: No point of the curve has a horizontal tangent line.
The tangent line is horizontal only at \( (-4, 1) \).
options.derivation: the point (-4, 1), where the numerator is 0, kept without checking that the denominator is also 0 there

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (-4, 1) \) and \( (4, 1) \).
options.derivation: the numerator's roots paired with y = 1 and reported without substituting into the curve

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (-4, 1) \) and \( (8, 1) \).
options.derivation: the denominator set to 0 instead of the numerator, which finds the points where y = v
